answer: Persistent contribution ledger. Each identity must maintain a continuous pulse of small, useful tasks; gaps reset its score. To sustain many identities, an attacker must spread limited labor across them, so each fake identity yields diminishing returns while demanding real, verifiable effort. The ledger also weighs rare inputs—like shale samples or timber surveys—that are costly to fake repeatedly, raising the marginal cost per sybil identity until it exceeds expected gain.
